BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Package Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary point:** The seller's note says [STANDARD] clauses have been "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and need no scrutiny. Nothing in our file shows Wattlebridge has agreed any of them. The labels are the seller's, so I have reviewed every item, including those marked [STANDARD]. Almost all of them conflict with our playbook.

## 1. Liability architecture

**General cap (Cl. 12.1): 20% / AUD 4.8m.** Our starting position is 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% figure is a fallback that requires prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying the draft, and none has been given. **Push back:** counter at 25% / AUD 6m. Do not concede 20% without that authority.

**Thresholds (Cl. 12.2).** The seller proposes a AUD 25,000 de minimis (ours is AUD 5,000), and a AUD 250,000 basket with recovery only of the excess (ours is AUD 50,000, with first-dollar recovery once exceeded). Under the seller's version, a AUD 240,000 breach is unrecoverable. **Push back:** de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar.

**Time limits (Cl. 12.3 / 13).** The seller proposes 18 months for general claims (ours is 24). Our 18-month fallback also needs Amelia Frost's written approval. The clause also provides that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise. This is a general-regime override of exactly the kind the playbook prohibits. **Push back:** 24 months for general claims; delete the "applies to all Claims" language; the regimes stay separate.

**Fundamental / Title.** The seller wants title and capacity warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is the most serious departure. Our position is a separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar. **Push back:** reject outright. Title and capacity are fundamental to what we are buying.

**Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (Cl. 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5).** These apply to "all Claims of any nature," and the package has no fraud carve-out. Our position carves fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one may waive that. **Push back:** insert the carve-out in full, with an express non-waiver statement.

## 2. Disclosure and knowledge

**Data-room and public-register disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1 and 1.2).** The seller discloses "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to" in the data room, plus the Accounts, statutory registers and public records. Our playbook requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. This clause would disclose almost anything and shift the risk to us. **Push back:** delete DL 1.1 and 1.2 as general disclosures. Disclosure must be specific and fairly presented against each warranty.

**Date of disclosure.** The letter speaks as at 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026, so the letter is stale. **Push back:** require a bring-down disclosure to signing and to Completion, with an updated data room index.

**Buyer knowledge (Cl. 8.3).** The clause excludes any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records." It is a blanket exclusion, which the playbook prohibits. **Push back:** delete it. If the seller needs a knowledge qualifier, it must name seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and it must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

## 3. Conditions and completion mechanics

**Bluefen (Cl. 3 / 6.3; DL 2).** Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). The seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's consent. The DL confirms no final written consent and no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied. Our playbook requires effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours are both unacceptable for a material customer consent. **Push back:** make effective Bluefen consent, with evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied, an express condition precedent to Completion.

**Riverlark (Cl. 2 / 7; DL 3).** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The seller will provide a release after Completion. That leaves a debt-like item with us, which conflicts with the debt-free/cash-free structure. Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. A post-completion release is only acceptable with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval. **Push back:** require a payoff letter and direct repayment at Completion, with releases delivered at Completion.

**Employee bonuses (DD-005; Funds flow; DL 5).** The seller says the AUD 420,000 bonuses are "a matter for the Seller" and are not itemised in the funds flow. The DL also says the disclosure does not address payroll tax, super or other on-costs. Our playbook requires the bonuses, plus triggered on-costs, either as a specific funds-flow line item or as seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them. **Push back:** add a specific line item or seller funding for the AUD 420,000 and all triggered on-costs, and add a specific indemnity. Confirm the on-cost position.

## 4. Specific matters

**Ironquay IP (Cl. 11.1; DL 4).** The seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it adequate. DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open, and the DL confirms there is no receipt or confirmatory assignment, and that transfer of SOW3 Project Materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified in either direction. **Push back:** broaden the indemnity to cover IP ownership and transfer defects generally, preserve the SOW3 cure, and require evidence of payment or a cure before Completion. Do not treat the AUD 180,000 as proven or disproven.

**Export/privacy incident (DD-006; Cl. 4.6 / Schedule 6; DL 6).** The seller calls this "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." The DL says a download link went to an unintended external address and the export may contain about 1,240 records with personal information (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). It does not establish whether anyone accessed the file, or whether notification is required. Our playbook assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand, in either direction. Neither side's characterisation is evidence. **Push back:** require log preservation, a completed investigation with a written report, regular updates, and a specific indemnity sitting outside the general regime. Do not accept "not material" and do not assert a breach.

**Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000; DL 8).** The seller calls these ordinary-course operating costs. The DL says it is unknown whether they are unavoidable, terminable or accrued. Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic debt classification or price deduction. **Push back:** request the contracts and assess them. Do not reclassify them as debt or deduct from price automatically.

**Tax and IP (seller note).** The seller says these are "settled under the general regime." They are not settled. Under the playbook they remain open, and we should assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. **Push back:** reject "settled" and keep Tax and IP as separate open categories, not subject to the general regime.

**Title (DL 10; DD-012).** The seller relies on the share register as proof of title. The playbook treats DD-012 as an internal supplied source, not independent proof. **Push back:** require independent evidence of title, encumbrances and authority. In Australia this would typically include ASIC company extracts, a PPSR search over the shares, and inspection of the register and any certified copies. The seller should give title warranties on that basis.

**Mossvale (DL 9) and office lease (DL 7).** The playbook does not address these. The DL indicates an assignment restriction and a notification obligation, but neither is said to require consent to the share sale. **Push back:** ask for a clear position on whether consent or notice is required for the share sale, and treat any consent as a closing item. Confirm our position with the deal team before taking a firm stance.

## 5. Gaps in the seller package

The package does not include the following playbook items at all:
- the fraud and deliberate-misconduct carve-out;
- a separate Fundamental/Title regime;
- specific indemnities for bonuses, Ironquay, the privacy incident and Riverlark;
- a bring-down of disclosure.

These should be added to our mark-up.

## 6. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the efficiency note.** Review every clause, including those marked [STANDARD].
2. **Caps and thresholds:** general cap 25% / AUD 6m; de minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar. Do not concede the 20% cap without Amelia Frost's written authority.
3. **Time limits:** 24 months for general claims. Delete the "applies to all Claims" language.
4. **Fundamental/Title:** separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
5. **Fraud carve-out:** insert in full, non-waivable.
6. **Disclosure:** specific fair disclosure only. Delete whole-data-room and public-register disclosure. Require a bring-down.
7. **Buyer knowledge:** delete Cl. 8.3. Any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry.
8. **Bluefen:** effective consent and evidence of conditions satisfied as a condition precedent to Completion.
9. **Riverlark:** payoff letter, direct repayment at Completion, releases at Completion.
10. **Bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a funds-flow line item or seller-funded, with a specific indemnity.
11. **Ironquay:** broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, require payment evidence or cure.
12. **Privacy incident:** preserve logs, investigate, require written updates, specific indemnity. Make no assumption of breach or quantum.
13. **Sandbar:** assess the contracts. No automatic debt classification or price deduction.
14. **Tax and IP:** keep open and separate. Reject "settled."
15. **Title:** require independent title, encumbrance and authority evidence. DD-012 is not sufficient.
16. **Mossvale and lease:** seek a clear position on consent versus notice; confirm our stance with the deal team.

Any concession outside these positions requires Amelia Frost's written approval identifying the draft.
